conclusions: The measure gaussianReal 0 1 assigns the singleton set {0} exactly zero mass in ENNReal: (gaussianReal 0 1)({0}) = 0.
mathematical_definitions: Let μ be the fixed measure gaussianReal 0 1 on the Borel real line.
The expression μ({0}) is the ENNReal-valued measure of the singleton containing the real number zero.
Because the second parameter is the nonzero NNReal value 1, gaussianReal 0 1 uses its density-defined branch rather than its Dirac branch.
translation.proposition_plain_english: The fixed nondegenerate Gaussian measure with parameters zero and one has no atom at the real number zero: the literal extended-nonnegative-real mass of the singleton {0} is zero.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition is closed: it has no quantified variables, hypotheses, or implication antecedents.
It concerns only the single fixed measure gaussianReal 0 1 and only the singleton {0}; it does not state the corresponding result for arbitrary parameters or arbitrary singleton points.
It asserts a literal equality in ENNReal, not merely equality after conversion to Real.
It does not itself state full atomlessness, absolute continuity, a density formula, a distribution-function identity, or any quantitative probability bound.
There is no antecedent whose inconsistency could make the proposition vacuously true.
ambiguities: The dependency information does not expand gaussianPDF, so the exact density formula and its normalization are not reconstructed.
Although the branch definition of gaussianReal is exposed, the intended statistical interpretation of its second NNReal parameter is not independently specified.
